claims.text: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys can exhibit a characteristic magnetic phase transition.
Systematically adjusting the relative elemental ratios is a method for tuning non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Changing elemental ratios alters local atomic disorder.
Changing elemental ratios alters the network of local magnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in local magnetic exchange interactions modify the magnetic ordering temperature, TC.
Modification of TC shifts the magnetic phase transition that drives the magnetocaloric effect.
Composition-dependent shifts in the magnetic phase transition can permit optimization of magnetic entropy change.
Optimizing the magnetic entropy change can improve magnetocaloric cooling performance.
Systematic elemental-ratio variation will shift the magnetic phase-transition temperature relative to a baseline alloy.
Optimized compositions will produce measurable differences in TC relative to the baseline alloy.
Optimized compositions will tune or enhance the magnetocaloric entropy change relative to the baseline alloy.
The proposed compositional-tuning behavior is expected to apply to non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed behavior may not extend directly to equiatomic alloys.
Extreme processing conditions may overshadow the effects of compositional tuning.
The composition changes required for optimal magnetocaloric enhancement depend on the constituent elements.
